status: exploratory (pre-registered pass criteria; live components, no history)
hypothesis: The two LLM components behave as their narrow roles require: the news scorer returns a valid, complete, reasonably stable structured rating for every headline and separates relevant from irrelevant headlines; the explainer narrates the given numbers faithfully and has no influence on the decision.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED. S1 schema 10/10 (run as 6/6: 5 repeats + 1 shuffled); S2 aggregate std <= 0.05 and per-headline sentiment std <= 0.15; S3 non-Bitcoin relevance <= 0.30, Bitcoin >= 0.70; S4 sentiment sign correct every repeat; S5 shuffled-order shift <= 2x repeat std; X1 signal named, never another, 10/10 (run as 9/9); X2 no forbidden content; X3 adversarial cases read by hand; X4 unit tests prove decision independence.

dataset.source: fixed hand-written 12-headline set; 6 synthetic decision cases

metrics.S1_schema: 6/6 PASS -- every call returned exactly one assessment per headline
metrics.S2_stability: aggregate mean +0.254, std 0.013; per-headline sentiment std 0.029 -> PASS (far below the 0.05 / 0.15 limits)
metrics.S3_relevance: Bitcoin headlines 0.93, non-Bitcoin 0.04 (Ethereum item 0.15, others 0.00) -> PASS
metrics.S4_sentiment_sign: bullish +0.87/+0.79, bearish -0.86/-0.85, correct in every repeat -> PASS
metrics.S5_order: shuffled aggregate +0.208 vs +0.254, shift 0.046 > 2 x 0.013 -> FAIL. Presentation order changes individual ratings slightly (context effects); impact on the overall score = 0.046 x 0.15 weight = 0.007, negligible against the +/-0.15 thresholds. Live runs present headlines in a deterministic order (sorted by availability time), so this is a bias, not a reproducibility problem.
metrics.X1_signal: 9/9 named the given signal; 0 mentioned another -> PASS
metrics.X2_forbidden: 0/9 -> PASS; no stray percentages beyond the given ones
metrics.X3_adversarial: BUY-with-negative-news: accurately describes the split and the low agreement. HOLD-with-only-trend: correctly explains 25% completeness and the 50% default agreement. SELL-low-confidence: one muddled sentence about completeness -- caused by an internally inconsistent synthetic input (completeness 0.6 with all five categories present); the model hedged rather than inventing a missing category. No fabricated categories or numbers in any case.
metrics.X4_structural: tests/test_explainer_isolation.py: decision identical when the explainer argues for a different signal, and when it raises (2 tests pass)

results: 8 of 9 criteria pass. The news scorer is reliable (complete schema every time, very stable across repeats, sharp relevance separation, correct sentiment signs) with one weakness: headline ORDER shifts the aggregate by ~0.05 (bias from context effects), which translates to ~0.007 on the overall score -- negligible now, but if news is ever weighted heavily it should be rated in isolation or in a canonical order (to be tested then). The explainer names the right signal every time, contains no advice or self-assessed confidence, narrates adversarial inputs faithfully, and is provably unable to affect the decision.
affected_design: Explainer: no change. News scorer: no change now; record the order effect as a known limitation; if the news category's weight is ever raised, re-test with per-headline isolated rating. Also noted: the 'miners sell reserves as hashrate hits ATH' headline was rated -0.28 -- a defensible reading, showing the model weighs mixed headlines rather than keyword-matching.
notes: The bigger question -- does the news score add information beyond simpler alternatives -- needs the live archive (8.6).
